info.title: Todos API
info.description:
Read and change the todo list kept by the Todos app on your Mac, from your other devices on your tailnet.

The API exists only while **Remote Access** is turned on in the app (Todos → Remote Access). Requests reach the Mac through `tailscale serve`, over HTTPS, at the address shown in that menu.

**On the Mac itself.** While the app runs, the same API is also served on a Unix domain socket that only your user can open: `~/Library/Application Support/Todos/todos.sock` (or `TODOS_SOCKET`). There it needs no token, and it is there whether Remote Access is on or off. This is how the `todos` command reaches the app. A few operations exist only on the socket, and a few only at the network address; each says so, and is marked `x-todos-only-on` (`socket` or `port`). Where an operation is not served, its path is answered exactly like one that does not exist.

**Authentication.** Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (Todos → Remote Access → Copy Access Token). Browsers sign in once at /login and use a session cookie instead. Only `GET /health` and `POST /session` work without it.

**Conflicts.** Every task has a `rev` that goes up by one with each change, whoever makes it (this API, the app, or a Claude session). Edits and deletes must name the rev they are based on in `If-Match`. If the task has moved on, you get 409 with the current task and nothing is changed. Adding a comment, adding or checking a subtask, and completing a task need no rev.

**Attribution.** Changes appear in the task's activity as made by you, labelled with the device (from Tailscale). API clients can name themselves with an `X-Todos-Client` header, e.g. `X-Todos-Client: iOS Shortcut`.

**Not available here.** Starting a Claude session on a task is only possible on the Mac itself: in the app, or from the `todos` command through the local socket (`/tasks/{id}/claude-session`).

**Claude sessions on another Mac.** A Mac can use another Mac's list instead of its own (Todos → Use Another Mac's List…). Its Claude sessions then change this list through the API, and say so with `X-Todos-Claude-Session`, so their changes are credited to them.

**Retries.** Any change can carry an `Idempotency-Key` header. Sending it again with the same key does nothing the second time, so a client can retry safely after a timeout.

**Compatibility.** `GET /meta` reports the API version and revision, and `GET /info` adds how old a client may be. Nothing is removed or changed within version 1; additions raise the revision.

**Habits.** Everything under `/habits` (revision 5). Check-ins are only ever added: a slot checked in twice, by two devices that did not know about each other, keeps both check-ins and counts once, and undoing names the check-ins it removes. Changes to habits are announced on `/events` as `habits`, separately from `change`.

**Errors** always look like `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`.

tags.name: Habits
tags.description: Routines to check in on, with streaks. Added in revision 5. A habit is done at set times of day (its slots) every day or on chosen weekdays, or a number of days a week. A habit day runs from the habit's `dayStart` (03:00 unless changed) to the next, so brushing at 00:30 counts for the evening before. Streaks are worked out by the server only, from the check-ins, so every client shows the same numbers.

get.description:
For checking compatibility before relying on anything else. Within version 1 things are only ever added, and each addition raises `revision`, so a client needs "version 1, revision N or later". Todos 1.4 has no `/meta`: a 404 here means revision 1.

Revision 2 (Todos 1.5) added this endpoint and `version` in `GET /tasks`. Revision 3 (Todos 1.6) added the `Idempotency-Key` header on every change, and `at` on `/capture` and `/capture/preview`. Revision 4 added `GET /info` and the local socket. Revision 5 added habits. Revision 6 (Todos 1.7) added the `X-Todos-Claude-Session` header on every change.

get.description:
What the health check at the server's root says, plus the oldest version of each kind of client that still works with this app. A client older than its entry should stop and ask to be updated. A kind of client that is not listed has no minimum.

The health check itself is `GET /health` at the root of the server (not under `/api/v1`), on the network address and on the local socket. It needs no authentication, and answers `status`, `appVersion` and `apiVersion` only, once the server is ready. At the network address it is answered to requests relayed by Tailscale only while Remote Access is on.

minClientVersions.description: Client kind to the oldest version that still works, e.g. `{"cli": "0.1.0", "ios": "1.0"}`.

get.description: A server-sent event stream. Sends `hello` on connect and `change` whenever anything in the list changes, each with `{"version": n}`. Fetch what you need again when one arrives. Since revision 5, `habits` is sent whenever a habit or a check-in changes, with `{"version": n, "habits": m}`: `habits` is the habits' own version, and `version` is still the list's, unchanged. A change to habits does not send `change`, and a change to tasks does not send `habits`. A comment line arrives every 25 seconds to keep the connection open. Browsers must rely on the cookie here, since EventSource cannot send headers.

get.description: Values given for one filter are alternatives (`priority=high,medium` is high or medium); different filters must all match. In the list's usual order unless `sort` says otherwise: in progress, blocked, to do, then done; open tasks by priority, then due date (undated last); done tasks by most recently finished. The same rules decide what the dashboard, the `todos` command and the iPhone app list. Tasks in a list leave out their activity log and carry a `comments` count instead.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: open (everything not done), all, or any of todo, in_progress, blocked, done. Several can be given, separated by commas.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: high, medium, low. Several can be given, separated by commas.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Tags, separated by commas, with or without a leading # or @. A task matches if it has any of them, or every one of them with `tagMode=all`. Several tags added in revision 7.

parameters.name: tagMode
parameters.description: Whether a task needs any of the tags in `tag`, or all of them. Added in revision 7.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project names, ignoring case, separated by commas. An empty value, or an empty entry as in `work,`, means no project. A name that has a comma in it still matches as a whole. Several projects added in revision 7.

parameters.name: assignee
parameters.description: me or claude. Both can be given, separated by commas.

parameters.name: due
parameters.description: overdue (open, and due before today), today, tomorrow, week (today through the next 7 days), none (no due date), any (has one), before:YYYY-MM-DD or after:YYYY-MM-DD (that day left out), or a date YYYY-MM-DD for everything due on or before it. tomorrow, before: and after: added in revision 7.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words that must all appear in the title, notes, project, tags or subtasks.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Keys separated by commas, each ascending unless it starts with -: status (in progress, blocked, to do, done), priority (ascending is high first, so the most important come first), due, created, updated, completed, title (ignoring case), project, id. A task with nothing to sort by, such as no due date or no project, comes last whichever way the key runs. Ties go to the lower id, so the order is the same every time. `default`, or leaving it out, is the usual order described above, and can follow other keys. An unknown key is refused with 400, naming the valid ones. Added in revision 7.

total.description: How many tasks match, before limit and offset.

version.description: The version of the whole list when this was read: the same number live updates announce. Added in revision 2.

get.summary: What would a Claude session on this task be started with?
get.description:
Only on the local socket. Returns exactly what the app's own **Start with Claude** button uses, for a program on the Mac that starts the session itself: run `claude <args...> -- <prompt>` in `folder`.

At the network address this path does not exist: starting a Claude session, and where folders are on the Mac, stay on the Mac.

200.description: What to start the session with.

prompt.description: The opening message for the session.

folder.description: Full path of the folder Claude should work in: the one the app remembers for the task's project, if it still exists. Null when the app would ask (no project, or no folder chosen for it yet).

args.description: The options to give `claude` before `--` and the prompt, e.g. `["--name", "Todo #12: Fix login", "--allowedTools", "mcp__todolist"]`.

claude.description: Where the app found the `claude` command on this Mac, or null if it found none.

403.description: Refused: the request carried reverse-proxy headers. Nothing relayed is answered on the local socket.

404.description: No such task, subtask or endpoint.

post.summary: Record that a Claude session was started on this task
post.description: Only on the local socket. Does what the app does after its own button has started a session: assigns the task to Claude, adds "Started with Claude from terminal" to its activity (naming the folder if one is sent), and remembers that folder for the task's project, so the app and the next `GET` suggest it. Send it once the session has been started.

folder.description: Full path of the existing folder the session was started in.

Or say `slot` and `day` for every check-in of that slot, `day` alone for every check-in that day, or `skip: true` for that day's skip; these work for today and yesterday. sessionCookie.name: todos_session
sessionCookie.description: Set by POST /session. Changes made with it must come from the app's own origin.

rev.description: Goes up by one with every change to the task.

due.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Also accepted on input: today, tomorrow, +3d, a weekday name, "oct 20". null clears it.

repeat.description: Completing a repeating task creates its next occurrence.

remindAt.description: When the Mac shows a reminder. Also accepted on input: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" (the Mac's local time), "tomorrow 9am", "+2h".

createdBy.description: "me", or the Claude session that created it.

TaskSummary.description: A task as it appears in lists: everything except the activity log, plus a count of comments.

by.description: "me", or a Claude session such as "Claude Code · my-repo".

via.description: The device or client, when the change did not come from the Mac app itself.

title.description: The line with dates and markers taken out. Empty if nothing else was left.

due.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Also accepted on input: today, tomorrow, +3d, a weekday name, "oct 20". null clears it.

code.description: Stable, for programs: unauthorized, forbidden, forbidden_host, forbidden_origin, forbidden_user, not_found, method_not_allowed, invalid, invalid_json, unknown_field, unsupported_media_type, too_large, precondition_required, conflict, rate_limited, busy, internal; and for habits: too_late, too_early, skip_limit, no_such_slot, archived.

HabitSlot.description: A time of day a habit is done at. Times are local and floating: 07:30 means 07:30 wherever the user is.

id.description: Stable, lower-case. Made from the name if left out when creating. Send it back when editing, so the slot keeps its history.

oneOf.description: Start of the window the slot belongs in, HH:MM. With `until`; the window may run past midnight.
When to be reminded again if it still is not done, HH:MM.

HabitSchedule.description: When a habit is meant to be done. A change counts from the day it is made (a new weekly target, from next week); earlier days keep the schedule they had. A habit counted in days cannot become one counted in weeks, or the other way round.

oneOf.description: Every day. A day counts when every slot has a check-in.
On those days of the week.

target.description: How many days a week, whichever they are. Weeks run Monday to Sunday.

oneOf.description: A number of days a week. It has no slots, and its streak is counted in weeks.

HabitCheckin.description: One event in a habit's history: a check-in (`done`) or a skipped day (`skip`). Events are never edited; undoing one adds an undo that names it.

day.description: The habit day it counts for, YYYY-MM-DD. For a skipped week, its Monday.

zone.description: The time zone it happened in.

by.description: "me", or the Claude session that logged it.

via.description: The device or client it came through. Absent for the Mac app itself.

backfilled.description: True when it was logged the day after.

reason.description: Why a day was skipped, if given.

key.description: The Idempotency-Key it was sent with, if any.

undone.description: In a history: true when it has been taken back.

HabitDay.description: One day of a habit with slots.

state.description: off: not scheduled, paused, or before the habit began. done: every slot has a check-in. skipped: a rest day. open: not done, and still loggable (today or yesterday). partial and missed: too late.

at.description: When it was first checked in.

checkins.description: The check-ins it has: what an undo would name. More than one when two devices both checked it in.

HabitSession.description: One day of a habit counted in weeks.

current.description: Days (or weeks) in a row that counted, up to now. Days that are off, skipped, or still open are passed over: they neither break it nor add to it.

best.description: The longest it has ever been.

oneOf.description: Yesterday is unfinished and there is a streak behind it. It survives if `missing` is logged for `day` before `until`.

week.description: For a habit counted in weeks: the Monday of the week that is one day short.

oneOf.description: The streak before this one, for saying kindly that it ended: its length and its last day (or, in weeks, its last week's Monday).

Habit.description: A habit, how today stands, and its streak. `today` and `yesterday` are a HabitDay for a habit with slots and a HabitSession for one counted in weeks, which also has `week` and `lastWeek`.

dayStart.description: When this habit's day begins, HH:MM. A check-in before it counts for the day before.

paused.description: A paused habit expects nothing, and its streak waits.

archived.description: Put away, with its history kept. Left out of the list unless asked for.

rev.description: Bumped on each edit to the habit itself. Check-ins do not change it.

week.description: Only for a habit counted in weeks: this week so far.

count.description: Days with a check-in. Two check-ins on one day count once.

whole.description: False for a week the habit began or was paused in. Such a week counts if it was met and is held against no one if not.

count.description: Days with a check-in. Two check-ins on one day count once.

whole.description: False for a week the habit began or was paused in. Such a week counts if it was met and is held against no one if not.

lastWeek.description: Only for a habit counted in weeks: last week, which can still change until Monday ends. Null when the habit began this week.

rates.description: How much of what was expected got done over the last 7, 30 and 365 days, from 0 to 1: slots checked in out of slots scheduled (in weeks: days out of the target). Skipped and paused days are left out, and an open day never counts against. Null when nothing was expected.

skipsLeft.description: How many more days (or weeks) could be skipped right now. At most 2 days in any 7 and 6 in any 30; one week in any 4.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes the request safe to send again, for a retry after the answer was lost or a change queued while offline. 8 to 64 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, unique to this change (a UUID works). A second request with the same key changes nothing and answers with the task as it is now; an edit repeated this way is not a conflict even though the first attempt moved the revision on. Added in revision 3.

ClaudeSession.name: X-Todos-Claude-Session
ClaudeSession.description: Sent by the MCP server when a Claude session works on this list from another Mac (one that uses this Mac's list). The change is credited to that session in the task's activity, as it would be had the session run here. Only names that start with "Claude" or "Cowork" count; anything else is recorded as yours. Like the device labels, it says who did something and grants nothing.
